# 1.2.42 - the chapter comes back round, and the windows stop lying

Two whole chapters were played in a running Foundry for this release - a GM and
three players, every gesture a click on something actually on the screen, nothing
called from the console unless a GM could only have reached it that way. That is
where almost everything below came from.

**The Class Trial could not be finished from the interface at all.** "Close and
count" did nothing: the vote stayed open, the verdict button stayed greyed out
because it is gated on the count, and "End of chapter" stayed greyed out because
it is gated on the verdict. The cause is one word. ApplicationV2 dispatches
centrally on `[data-action]` and handles `close` itself - it is what the window
header's X uses - so a footer button carrying that action never reaches DialogV2's
submit at all, and the handler behind it was unreachable. Measured both ways:
press it with three ballots in and `voteClosed` stays false with no tally card;
rename the action and nothing else, and the count runs. Every other
`action: "close"` in the module is a literal Close whose handler returns null
anyway. This was the only one with work to do.

**The loop did not close either.** Ending a chapter moved the clock to chapter 2
and left the campaign in `phase: "classTrial"` with the debate floor open. The GM
was then told "The debate is open - Nonstop Debate." and pointed back at the trial
they had just finished, while every player's HUD read "Chapter 2 - Day 2 - Class
Trial". The way out existed the whole time, one button below the one they had
pressed, and nothing anywhere said so. The End of chapter screen closes the trial
itself now, and the panel's suggestion line learned the state it could not see.

**And the new chapter opens in the morning.** That screen moved the chapter and
the session and nothing else, so the next chapter began at whatever time of day
the trial ended - which is Night, because that is when murders happen - with
everybody's actions still spent from before the murder. Measured across two
chapters: chapter 1 finished at Day 1, Night and chapter 2 opened at Day 1, Night
with one student still holding an action from the time of day before. There is a
checkbox for the following morning now, refilling through the same call every
other advance uses. Both chapters now close on Day 2, Morning with full actions.

**The vote was counting people wrong.** Ballots went out per student rather than
per person: a player holding two students got two windows, and only one of them
could ever count because the tally is keyed by the sender. And `studentActors()`
includes the dead, so the victim of the murder being tried was handed a ballot -
at one player to one character, that is the murdered player voting in the trial
about their own death. Three players at the table were announced to the room as
four. Now three ballots for three players, one window each, and "3 of 3 votes"
counted out of what actually went out. `TRIAL.deadCastBallots` is where to change
your mind about the second half.

**Re-sending the ballots used to eat the votes already cast**, silently, and it
was the default button on that window - so the way to lose the room's votes was to
open the screen to see who had not answered yet and press Enter. The default
follows the state now: once the ballots are out it is "Close and count", and
starting over says what it will cost first.

**Six GM windows were photographs.** The Incident tracker was the worst of them:
it is the console for the fastest scene in the game, watched while the players
drive it from their own sheets, and it read "turn 1, victim to act, 5/5 Health,
6/6 Sanity" through a crisis action, through the victim dying, and through the
murder being closed - after which it stayed on screen still offering to close the
murder. The same measurement was then run on every other window that shows
something the world can move:

    Room setup         search tokens 3 -> 2 while the cell said 3
    Despair Flow       spilled Despair 95 -> 100 while the line said 95
    Give / take items  Usables 1/3 with two of them in the actor
    Projects           a project at 0/4 that had reached 1/4
    Trial evidence log "5 presented this chapter" with six in the world

In four of the five, the thing that moves the number is a player - so no hook on
the GM's own client was ever going to notice. Read-outs are swapped and rebuilt;
numbers that sit inside a form are written in place instead, because swapping
those would discard whatever the GM had typed and not applied.

**The scene rail stands on its own glass.** Three faults, each found by making the
solver print its own numbers: the mid seam landed inside the rail, the band was
sized to the rail's box rather than to the tiles in it, and the rail was bounded to
the notice tile's box instead of its leaned pane. Corners on their own shard, left
rail, tools shut then open: 2560x1440 went to 48/48 and 80/80, 1920x1080 to 46/48
and 76/80, 1600x900 to 38/48 and 61/80, and at 140% interface scale every reading
improved, including the right rail at 1920x1080 going 47/64 to 63/64.

**The tiles sit under the GM button.** The gap between them was 37px at 1920x1080,
16 at 1600x900 and 73 at 2560x1440 - three different holes from one constant, which
is what a number read in the wrong frame looks like. It is corrected after the
rotations now, against the gap the tiles keep between themselves rather than
against a number: 8/7, 7/6, 8/7, and 8/9 at 140%.

**The Investigation window spoke two vocabularies.** A planned Key Remnant reached
its finder as "Trace" with no description, because the planner collected a GM note
and had nowhere to put the words a player reads. The Final Truth Remnant had the
same gap and no "found by" line at all. Both take a name and a player description
now, the Final tab says who has copied it, and the End of chapter screen offers the
three clean-ups that were previously only reachable from a window a GM opens
mid-case.

**Smaller, and each one measured:** the chat card's header no longer overflows its
226px cell - the recipient list ellipsises and the speaker's name never shrinks,
131px over becomes 0; an intermittent `isGM` crash on a player's client was caught
with a stack and all five socket handlers are guarded; the scrim under the always-on
HUD blocks stopped drawing a slanted black card behind them, because a radial
gradient sizes itself to the corners by default and the fade was still painting when
it ran off the edge; Hope is the same star in the player's corner strip as in the
sheet's header, instead of the base theme's diamond; and the Key Remnant shortfall
says what the class actually turned up rather than "4 Key Remnants short of four
were never found", which is not a sentence.

Suite: 128 passed, 0 failed.

## Known, and deliberately left

The scene rail's last stragglers at 1080p and 900p stand on the notice tile's
glass. Foundry's control column is 314px and cannot wrap, so between the GM button
and that pane a 1080p screen is about 50px short and a 900px screen about 130.
Closing it means moving the notice tile down, which is a layout decision rather
than a partition one. Four shapes of the fix were built, measured and reverted;
what each one cost is written in the source so the next attempt starts from there.

Advancing the time of day still goes through the full campaign editor, with the
refill checkbox off by default. It is the most repeated gesture in a session and
it deserves one button; it did not get one this round.

A GM who never opens the Key Remnant planner is still billed the full Despair
shortfall when the trial starts, with no warning on the way in.
